description: Repo-standard IEEE 1364-2005 conformance surface for the strict verilog_2005 dialect profile on grammars/systemverilog.ebnf: (1) the curated accept/reject corpus matrix across all three SV dialect profiles, (2) the 0-profile-orphan wellformedness lint lock, (3) the profiled certificate-coverage baseline, deterministic across seeds. Owned by task tree VERILOG-2005-PROFILE (leaf .4.3).

cert.baseline_note: BASELINE pins, not a closure claim: under the strict subset profile the gated SV-only surface is profile-unreachable (the cert run itself classifies 287 of the 319 UNKNOWN as NO-reach-path dead-rule candidates under verilog_2005) — the expected posture per the tree's .1 D4 closure bar. Re-pinned 826/310 -> 817/319 at VERILOG-2005-PROFILE.6.2 (2026-07-02, PGEN-VERILOG-2005-PROFILE-0012): the SV-0025/SV-0027 leak fixes removed the 9 FALSE witnesses that had been earned through the leaked SV-only surface (time_literal, time_unit, unbased_unsized_literal, and the 6 time-unit keyword tokens) — witness dropping on a leak fix is the honest direction, and kw_n_1step itself moved from reachable-through-the-leak to NO-reach. Ratcheting the genuine remainder is its own follow-up work; drift in EITHER direction fails this gate and requires a re-baselined contract in the same commit.

cases.note: `-> e;` is the legal IEEE 1364-2005 event trigger.

The ~48 SV-only reserved words (`bit`, `int`, `class`, ...) are legal IEEE 1364-2005 identifiers (the D2 un-reserve axis); the sv_2017/sv_2023 `reject` rows are spec-correct because those words ARE reserved there. `initial assert (1);` is a legal 1364-2005 task enable of a task named `assert`.
The minimal module; also the alias-normalization accept probe.
Legal 1364-2005 task enable of a user task named `wait_order` (un-reserved under the profile).
A net named `logic` is legal IEEE 1364-2005; `logic` is a reserved word under the SV profiles (spec-correct rejects there). Regression lock for the `.4.1` over-rejection closed in `.4.2`.

SV-0022 waiver: the spec-valid single-semi `bind` never parses under ANY profile (pre-existing double-`semi` grammar defect), so the sv_2017/sv_2023 rows are also `reject`; re-adjudicate to `accept` when SV-0022 lands. The verilog_2005 `reject` remains the profile-correct expectation either way.
The first SV-only family gated (`.2`); also the alias-normalization reject probe.

`#1step` delay_value is IEEE 1800-only (A.2.2.3); IEEE 1364-2005 delay_value is unsigned_number | real_number | identifier, and a faithful 1364-2005 lexer cannot even form `1step`. Reject-lock for the `SV-0025` fix (`.6.2`): before the fix this wrongly ACCEPTED under `verilog_2005` via the un-gated `delay_value` branch.
`#10ns` time-literal delay is IEEE 1800-only; 1364-2005 has no time literals. Second `SV-0025` reject-lock (the `time_literal` sibling branch of the same `delay_value_sv_only` lift).

`-> #5 e;` is legal in NEITHER dialect per the LRMs, but currently ACCEPTS under sv_2017/sv_2023 (SV-0023 mis-encoding of the `->>` delay form onto `->`); the sv-side `accept` rows record that defect posture — re-adjudicate when SV-0023 lands. verilog_2005 REJECT via the `event_trigger_control_sv_only` gate.

A time literal as an expression primary (`assign w = 10ns;`) is IEEE 1800-only. Reject-lock for the `SV-0027` fix (`.6.2`): `primary_literal`'s SV-only `time_literal` branch was un-gated under `verilog_2005`.

An unbased-unsized literal (`'0`, IEEE 1800 §5.7.1) does not exist in IEEE 1364-2005. Second `SV-0027` reject-lock (the `unbased_unsized_literal` sibling branch of the same `primary_literal_sv_only` lift).

Uses the non-reinterpretable `assert (1) else $error(...)` action-block form: a bare `initial assert (1);` is a legal 1364-2005 task enable (see the accept corpus), per feedback_corpus_expected_from_spec_not_fix.
Pinned on the ANSI form `input interconnect w` until SV-0024 (un-braced non-ANSI `port_expression` list over-acceptance, `module m (a b);`) lands.
Uses `return x;` (argument form): a bare `return;` is a legal 1364-2005 task enable of a task named `return`, per feedback_corpus_expected_from_spec_not_fix.
Uses the `else`-action form task enables cannot take; a plain `wait_order (a, b);` is a legal 1364-2005 task enable (see the accept corpus).
